correctness.rationale: At every common absolute height 2u the washer integrand is s²(q(t/s)−q(u/s)). Equality of complete volume functions is exactly the equation ∫₀ᵘ H_s(t)dt=uH_s(u) for H_s=q−s²q(·/s). Continuity makes the left hand side C¹, so dividing by u>0 legitimates differentiating H_s and yields H_s'=0. The constant from u=0 gives the multiplicative equation, including the t=1 limit. Changing variables gives exact log-periodicity on y≥0. Extending a continuous periodic function to the real line preserves each other positive period (shift any pair sufficiently far right by the first period); the dense additive subgroup for two irrationally related periods forces constancy. The tip condition then fixes the spheroid coefficient. For commensurate scales the sine perturbation has exactly the required common period and q''≤−2+ε hypot(2−ω²,3ω)<0; q'(0)=0 and q(1)=0 give strict decrease and positivity inside. The square-root profile is strictly concave, and its even extension gives a strictly convex solid by the norm triangle inequality. Bounded second derivatives through the equator give C¹,¹ there; smooth inversion of q at the tip, as a function of squared radial distance, gives smooth tip charts. With a second-order Taylor expansion a single period forces the linear coefficient to vanish and gives a limiting value at infinity, so that period already forces constancy.
residual_risks: No assertion for one isolated height, finitely many sampled heights at a scale, noisy equality, noncoaxial bores, or nonmonotone profiles. The numerical example is a diagnostic; the analytic argument establishes exact equality at all heights for the commensurate pair.
